entry.name: Voxel Noise
entry.qfep_connection: 3D noise made walkable census: cubes appear where the field crosses threshold, vanish where it does not. The invisible correlation structure of the noise stands revealed as architecture — you are looking at the field's memory, cell by cell.

dna.fixture_why: Every visible parameter of this room is driven off a clock in _process — time, time_scale, cloud_density and both colours all move — so a still is taken at whatever instant the shutter happened to fall. `frozen` leaves the .tscn's own authored uniforms in place and never advances them, which makes four basis frames comparable instead of four different moments. It is a String enum, not a bool, because the sweep sets exports from strings before _ready and a typed bool silently rejects "true" — the trap that has eaten fixture flags twice. `live` is the default and is the shipped behaviour, so no placement sees the pin.
dna.default: generator=perlin - the perlin branch of the shader's dispatch is the shipped noise2d body, character for character (diffed against HEAD, not eyeballed), and _apply_generator writes 1 into a uniform whose own declared default is already 1. Note the default is perlin and NOT simplex, the opposite of the bench artifacts, because that is what this file has always computed: hash2 returns a gradient per lattice corner and the interpolation dots it with the offset, which is Perlin's construction with a sine hash instead of a permutation table. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 13 mentions across 11 map files, not the 5 the promotion brief carried, by three reach-paths - bare tokens in Noise_6_Wall, Corridor_Noise_6_Wall, Noise_Functions, TestMap_Unused_23 and Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:shader_noise_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value and the # keys are the furniture's; and `perlin_noise->shader_noise_space` in Trial_erosion_noise, which is a transformation target and not a config. None carries a generator key, and apply_grid_config returns unless a token names a word this file knows AND that word differs from the one it holds.
dna.was: seven exports, every one of them a rate or a toggle on the animation loop, and the runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The decision that carries the argument was not an export at all: it was the body of a single function called noise2d, hard-coded to one basis in a room whose walls, ceiling and floor are made of nothing else.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order. The noise sequence is built on comparing bases; spelling the comparison a second way would leave nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. What differs here is the scale of the question: on the bench a basis is a tabletop of displaced cubes you look down at, and here it is the room you are standing inside.
dna.amplitude_note: The four bases are AMPLITUDE-MATCHED rather than merely swapped in. Measured over 30,000 samples each returns mean |value| = 0.137, which is what the shipped perlin returns; the three scaling constants in the shader (0.770, 38.0, 0.827) exist only for that. Without them the sweep would mostly have been reading which basis is BRIGHTER once the six-octave sum is pushed through smoothstep(0.2, 0.8), and the axis would have been about exposure instead of about structure. Their own characters survive the matching: measured local step per unit distance is 4.7% of mean for value, 8.4% perlin, 11.0% cellular, 13.9% simplex.
dna.declined: animation_speed (this file's own declared critical_parameter until now), time_scale_variation, color_cycle_speed and density_variation - four rates, all real, all audible in the room, and all invisible to one still. Promoting any of them would have produced the info_board result: a finished-looking experiment answering nothing. `octaves` was also declined despite simplex_noise carrying it as a numeric axis: the fbm here runs six octaves over a wall two metres from the eye, so the lower rungs would read as a blurrier wall rather than as a claim about self-similarity, and one honest axis is worth more than a second one that argues about resolution.
dna.still_note: the basis is a fragment-shader uniform, so it is resolved every frame and never settles into geometry — but it is also constant in time under the fixture, so one frame is a complete account. The subject is a closed 16 x 12 x 27 m box of CSGBox3D walls with cull_disabled, so the sweep's camera sits outside and photographs two or three wall faces filling the frame. That is the field at full size, which is the best case for measuring a basis; if the bite comes back small, suspect the clock, not the axis.
dna.finding: QueerNoiseShader.gdshader and WallNoiseShader.gdshader were BYTE-IDENTICAL, header comment included — the room-sphere shader carried the wall shader's filename at the top of the file. The @identity's claim that 'the two materials run independent shader noise loops' out of phase is one shader run twice with different uniform values and a 0.7x offset on time. Both files now carry the same dispatch so the room and its walls change basis together.

entry.name: noisesphere
entry.qfep_connection: A hemisphere deformed by noise and dressed in the planet shader: a world's skin grown from correlation. The dome overhead is the chapter's quiet claim to scale — planets are noise seen from far enough away.

dna.default: generator=simplex, octaves=4 - octaves=4 is the shipped @export byte for byte. generator=simplex does NOT assign a noise type: the shipped file set frequency and fractal_octaves and never touched noise_type at all, so this ground has always been whatever basis FastNoiseLite itself defaults to, and _build_noise leaves it alone at the default value instead of assigning TYPE_SIMPLEX - assigning it would be a silent correction that reshapes the terrain under every existing placement. MEASURED, not assumed: there are 11 mentions across 10 map files, by three reach-paths - bare tokens in Corridor_Noise_Space_10, Noise_Space_10 and Walk_grande_galerie_axial_text; `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:noise_space` in six museum trials, where the token is the furniture's mount value and the # keys are the furniture's; and `simplex_noise->noise_space` plus `noise_space->noisetorus` in Trial_erosion_noise, which are transformation targets and not config. None carries a generator or octaves key, and apply_grid_config returns without regenerating unless a key is present AND its value differs from the one the node already holds.
dna.was: an artifact named for its noise that never said which noise, and three @exports nobody could reach. TopologySpace has no apply_grid_config and NoiseSpace had none either, so noise_scale, octaves and persistence were editor-only: every placement got the same 10 x 10 m landform and map_data could not say otherwise. The runner refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS on exactly that ground - the knobs existed, nothing was connected to them.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, shader_noise_space, noise_terrain - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order and the same default. cellular, not worley, for the same reason: the noise sequence is built on comparing bases, and spelling the comparison four ways would leave nothing to compare. `octaves` is simplex_noise's word for the same quantity, but the ladder is 1-2-3-4 rather than its 1-2-4-6, and the difference was computed rather than chosen: this mesh samples every 0.1 m across a 10 m space (resolution 100) while the base wavelength is about 2 m (frequency 0.1 against coordinates pre-multiplied by noise_scale 5.0), so octave k has wavelength 2 / 2^(k-1) and octaves 5 and 6 land at 0.125 and 0.0625 m, below the mesh's 0.2 m Nyquist wavelength. Declaring 6 would ship a rung that differs from 4 only by aliasing at a sixteenth of the amplitude.
dna.vocabulary_declined: readout (relief|plate|column), carried by perlin_noise, simplex_noise, perlin_noise_terrain, random_edge_profile and mandelbrot_set. Declined for exactly the reason noise_terrain recorded when it declined the same word: readout asks a geometric question about a tabletop field, and this is a walkable substrate with a trimesh collider under it, so plate and column would change what the player STANDS ON rather than what the field claims to be, and the word would stop meaning one thing across the sequence. noise_terrain's own second axis `legend` (contours|relief|mood) is declined too, for the opposite reason: there both encodings already existed in the file and only a 2D button chose between them, while here there is exactly one material - a flat organic-green StandardMaterial3D with no height encoding at all - so the shipped look is neither contours nor relief nor mood, and taking the word would mean inventing a fourth value to hold the thing that actually ships. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary.
dna.still_note: both axes resolve during _ready and never move again - the noise object is fully configured before the 10,201-vertex mesh is built, and nothing on this artifact animates - so a single frame is a complete account of both. Deterministic besides: FastNoiseLite is left on its default seed and nothing in the file calls randf(), so four generator frames are four bases over one footprint rather than four landscapes, and no seed pin is needed.
dna.framing_note: the subject is a 10 x 10 m slab carrying about 4 m of relief, and a fit-by-diagonal camera is roughly right for it (the plan diagonal and the box diagonal are within 4% of each other), so no numeric framing is set. If the bite reads modest, compare silhouettes before believing it: expect cellular to be the loudest value by far and octaves=1 to be the smoothest.
dna.repair: persistence has been an @export since the file was written and was never spent on anything. It is the fBm gain and is now wired to fractal_gain - but only when it differs from its own shipped 0.5, so a placement that never names it leaves the noise object untouched no matter what FastNoiseLite's own default gain is. It is a repair, not a declared axis.

entry.qfep_connection: The chapter's thesis as a place: a whole environment driven by configurable noise, walked from inside. Not an exhibit about noise — an exhibit *made of* it, where changing a parameter re-decides the room around you.

entry.description: Interactive Simplex noise generation and visualization for high-quality procedural content
entry.name: Simplex Noise
entry.qfep_connection: Perlin's own second draft: the simplex grid replaces squares, fewer artifacts, better behavior in high dimensions. Standing beside its ancestor it teaches versioning as a mathematical practice — even noise gets revised.

dna.default: generator=simplex, readout=relief - both are exactly what the shipped code did (NoiseVisualizer hard-coded FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX and lifted a uniform cube to its sample), so the 7 existing placements render identically
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: simplex_noise - readout is the same axis with the same three values and the same default on both, so the pair can be compared instead of merely contrasted
dna.was: no exports on the root at all - the sweep refused it as NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The two decisions that carry the argument sat one node down as constants: which basis fills the field, and whether a sample is read as elevation or as measurement. Note that the artifact called Perlin Noise has been drawing SIMPLEX noise since it was written; the promotion makes that a declared choice (generator=perlin is now available) rather than silently correcting it and rewriting seven maps.

entry.description: Interactive Perlin noise generation and visualization
entry.name: Perlin Noise
entry.qfep_connection: Perlin's gift to graphics: gradients on a lattice, interpolated smoothly — randomness that flows instead of stutters. Every organic-looking surface in games descends from this trick. The demo hands you the dials: octaves stacking detail, persistence deciding how loudly the small scales speak.
